newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Rate rethink boosts dollar, bourses mixed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Rate rethink boosts dollar, bourses mixed.

text.p: The dollar returned to the attack in Europe on Thursday as foreign exchange markets appeared to give the U.S. Federal Reserve the benefit of the doubt after it held interest rates unchanged.
The London and Frankfurt stock exchanges drifted higher in early trading, but disappointing results from French heavyweight stocks Lyonnaise des Eaux and LVMH weighed on the Paris bourse.

Strong British government bonds, or gilts, traded steady after economic data showed the August non-EU deficit narrowed from July. German government bonds also firmed, buoyed by news that Bonn did not intend to issue more 10 or 30-year debt this year.
The German mark came under fire from the dollar, which strengthened by nearly a pfennig, and other European currencies in early European trade.
The Italian lira, which hit two-year peaks against the mark on Wednesday, led the way up for high-yielding currencies, which were also boosted by sales of the yen.

Although the market seemed to have accepted the Fed's decision this week to keep monetary policy steady, analysts said the market would scrutinise U.S. August durable goods data due at 1230 GMT to assess whether it was correct. U.S. weekly jobless claims are also due at 1230 GMT.

"The danger is that if the durable goods are considerably stronger than the market is going for...that would be a signal the Fed had taken too many risks and perhaps the lack of action was politically rather than economically inspired," said Stephen King, deputy chief economist at HSBC James Capel in London.
Economists forecast the figures would show durable goods fell an average of 0.1 percent after rising 1.7 percent in July.
The dollar was quoted at 1.5191 marks and 110.63 yen by 0930 GMT, up from late Wednesday's European level of 1.5112 marks and 110.40 yen.
Klaus Baader, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said a weaker than expected durable goods figure could weigh on the dollar.

"It would mean rate hikes in the U.S. are not merely delayed -- as the market is currently inclined to think -- but increasingly disappearing off the agenda, and that I think is going to put downward pressure on the dollar," Baader said.
London's FTSE 100 continued Wednesday's rally, supported by gilts and bonds, coupled with Wall Street's modest rebound on Wall Street overnight.
By 0930 GMT, the leading FTSE 100 index was up five points, having gained 25.2 on Wednesday.
"Yesterday's move surprised everyone, and I think we could see a bit more of a squeeze this morning," said one dealer.
But he added the upside may be limited as institutional funds do not yet seem quite ready to dive back into British equities.
France's blue chip CAC-40 index weakened a few points in early trading as some stocks took a hammering from investors after reporting disappointing first-half results.
German DAX opened bourse trade higher, buoyed by Wall Street's three point gain, supported by the firmer dollar and the U.S. bond rally.
Volumes continue to be limited, but corporate news boosted individual shares. Schering rose 1.80 marks to 118.90 after saying it might pay a two-mark dividend in 1996.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.5191 marks and 110.63 yen by 0930 GMT, up from late Wednesday's European level of 1.5112 marks and 110.40 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 5.2 points at 3,940.9.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 1.78 points at 2,101.63.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 7.28 points at 2.666.25. PRECIOUS METALS
GOLD was slightly weaker in early Europe at $382.40 versus $382.65 at the London close. Silver was two cents lower at $4.90.
